AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: In view of paucity of studies on Central post stroke pain (CPSP), in this hospital based prospective study; we evaluated the frequency, spectrum, imaging and Quantitative sensory testing in cohort of stroke patients with CPSP.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Stroke patients who developed CPSP at onset or during follow up were included. Patients were subjected to clinical evaluation and sensory testing. Severity of stroke were defined by Modified Rankin scale (MRS) and disability by Barthel Index. Quantitative sensory testing included monofilament testing and evaluation for static and dynamic mechanical allodynia, punctuate hyperalgesia, temporal summation, cold allodynia and cold hyperalgesia. Sleep, anxiety and depression were also evaluated. Patients were treated with Pregabalin 150-600 mg/d and good response defined as >50% improvement in VAS score. CPSP symptoms were correlated with demographic information, sensory findings and imaging findings.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 319 patients with stroke were evaluated. CPSP occurred in 66 (20.7%) of them. Median age of CPSP patients was 55 (range 25-80) years. 31.8% patients were females. Onset, duration and distribution of pain were variable. Severity of symptoms did not correlate with demographic variables and site of lesion. Spino- thalamic sensations were normal in 42.3% patients. On treatment with pregabalin (150-600 mg) half of the patients had good response.

AbstractText.Label: DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: CPSP was present in 20.7% of stroke patients. Spinothalamic tract dysfunction may not be necessary for development of CPSP and it can be seen with normal spinothalamic sensation also. Location of stroke, its type and quality and severity of CPSP was not related.
